name: Moisture sandwiching

card.summary: A skincare layering routine, applying thin hydrating products to damp skin and sealing with thicker ones, aimed at plumper, more hydrated-looking skin.
card.note: Dermatologists differ on whether repeated misting adds benefit.

quick.overview:
Moisture sandwiching is a skincare routine where hydrating layers go onto damp skin, typically thin and watery products first, thicker creams last, so the thicker layer holds the water in. A TikTok version mists the face between steps.

The appearance goal is smoother, dewier, less flaky skin, especially for dry or irritated skin. No peer-reviewed study of the routine itself was located; dermatologists quoted in the press disagree on how much repeated misting helps.
quick.how: After cleansing, products are applied while the skin is still damp, light textures before heavy ones, finishing with moisturiser. The social media variant sprays a facial mist between layers. Some dermatologists suggest it can buffer irritation from active ingredients.
quick.risks: Low risk. One dermatologist notes oil-based products do not mix with water on the skin and that sunscreen is advised on dry skin; too much water-based mist may dilute actives.

lead: Moisture sandwiching is a skincare technique that layers hydrating products on damp skin, ordinarily from thinnest to thickest, so that a heavier moisturiser seals in the water below it. A popular SkinTok version, covered by Bustle, sprays a hydrating mist between steps, giving a routine like mist, serum, mist, moisturiser.[1]
The aim is hydrated, soft-looking skin and, for people using irritating actives, a cushion against dryness. Clarins describes it as suited to dry and dehydrated skin.[2]

Dermatologists quoted in the press differ on repeated misting: Dr. Hadley King supports one mist step but sees no need for repetition, while Dr. Brian Hibler says the extra layers have not been shown to improve hydration or penetration.[1]

angle.text: It targets the look of dry or dull skin by trapping water with layered products. Users report a dewier surface and less tightness.

paras: The principle is to apply products while the skin retains water from cleansing or mist, then cover with an occlusive or thick cream. The Bustle version cleanses, mists, applies serum, then moisturiser, with a mist between layers.[1] Experts quoted advise moisturiser soon after the mist, within about 30 seconds in one case.[1]

King says moisturiser is needed to lock in a mist's hydration.[1] Hibler says oil-based products will not mix with sprayed water, and that sunscreens should not be applied to damp skin or may be less effective.[1]
